sources: Winter, K. G., Rotta, J. C., and Smith, K. G., Studies of the Turbulent Boundary Layer on a Waisted Body of Revolution in Subsonic and Supersonic Flow, ARC R&M 3633, August 1968 (published 1970), https://reports.aerade.cranfield.ac.uk/handle/1826.2/2902
page: Table 1, printed page 21, phi = 0 rows; body equations in Fig. 1
format: Headerless CSV: X [in], Cp, M_delta, 1000 cf. Empty cf at X=15 in is missing, not zero. Numbers copied unchanged from the supplied checked transcription build/axisym/rm_m17.csv.
normalization: cf uses local edge dynamic pressure; Cp uses freestream dynamic pressure
trip: 0.005 in ballotini at 1.5 in from nose; inadequate at M >= 1.4 (section 3.4)
not_stated_by_source: wall thermal condition; the analysis assumes zero heat transfer
comparison_assumptions: T0=310 K with 290 and 330 K sensitivities
wall Cp used as edge Cp
edge total pressure from Taylor-Maccoll 20 degree cone
compare available cf only at X >= 12 in
transcription_checks: 28 Cp/M_delta rows imply p0_delta/p0_inf=0.9926-0.9962; Taylor-Maccoll predicts about 0.9957. Last body segment is cubic; junction residual must be below 1e-5.
